newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Israel keeping close eye on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Israel keeping close eye on Iraq.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel was following events in Iraq on Tuesday but would continue with life as normal.

"We've no special signs that point to any special problem from the standpoint of Israel and so there is no reason for making any special preparations from a public standpoint," Netanyahu told reporters after the U.S. launched a missile attack on Iraq.

"We are following the events. We are in close contact with the government of the United States and should there be a need for any kind of action, we'll take it," he said after meeting German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe.

Baghdad launched dozens of Scud missile attacks on Israel while battling a U.S.-led alliance during the 1991 Gulf War. Israelis sought shelter in sealed rooms and donned gas masks for fear the missiles might carry chemical warheads. Washington is Israel's closest ally.

U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk briefed the Israeli leader within minutes after the United States said it had launched cruise missile attacks against air defence targets to retaliate for Iraqi attacks in the Kurdish north.

The United States last sent cruise missiles against Iraq in June 1993 to avenge an alleged plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush during a visit to Kuwait. The attacks then killed six civilians.
